title.zh: 卷五十九 吳書十四 吳主五子傳
title.en: Volume 59: Book of Wu 14 - Biographies of the five sons of the Lord of Wu
title.raw: 卷五十九 吳書十四 吳主五子傳 Volume 59: Book of Wu 14 - Biographies of the five sons of the Lord of Wu

sentences.zh: 孫登字子高，權長子也。

translations.literal: Sun Deng, courtesy name Zigao, was Sun Quan's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng, whose courtesy name was Zigao, was the eldest son of Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 魏黃初二年，以權爲吳王，拜登東中郎將，封萬戶侯，登辭疾不受。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu of Wei, Sun Quan was made King of Wu; Deng was appointed General of the Household Gentlemen of the East and enfeoffed as marquis of ten thousand households, but Deng declined on grounds of illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei’s second Huangchu year, Cao Wei invested Sun Quan as King of Wu, named Sun Deng General of the Household Gentlemen of the East, and offered him a fief of ten thousand households; Sun Deng pleaded illness and refused the title.

sentences.zh: 是歲，立登爲太子，選置師傅，銓簡秀士，以爲賔友，於是諸葛恪、張休、顧譚、陳表等以選入，侍講詩書，出從騎射。

translations.literal: That same year Deng was established as heir apparent. Tutors were chosen and installed, outstanding scholars were selected and appointed as guest companions, and thus Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others entered by selection, attending him in the study of the Classics and histories and accompanying him in riding and archery when he went out.
translations.idiomatic: The same year he was made crown prince. Sun Quan picked tutors for him, sifted talented men to serve as his companions, and Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others were chosen to join him—indoors they lectured on the poetry and histories; outdoors they drilled riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 權欲登讀《漢書》，習知近代之事，以張昭有師法，重煩勞之，乃令休從昭受讀，還以授登。

translations.literal: Sun Quan wished Deng to read the Han shu and become familiar with recent affairs. Because Zhang Zhao had a proper method of instruction and Sun Quan was reluctant to burden him excessively, he ordered Zhang Xiu to receive instruction in reading from Zhang Zhao and then return to teach Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wanted Sun Deng to read the Han shu and learn recent history. Zhang Zhao was the acknowledged master for that kind of reading, but Sun Quan hesitated to overwork him, so he had Zhang Xiu study under Zhang Zhao and then pass the lessons on to Sun Deng.

sentences.zh: 登待接寮屬，略用布衣之禮，與恪、休、譚等或同輿而載，或共帳而寐。

translations.literal: When Deng received his staff and subordinates, he broadly employed the courtesies of commoners: with Ke, Xiu, Tan, and the others he sometimes rode in the same carriage or slept under the same canopy.
translations.idiomatic: When he met his staff, he kept the manners of a private gentleman rather than a palace heir—he rode in the same carriage with Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, and Gu Tan, and sometimes shared a tent and slept beside them.

sentences.zh: 太傅張溫言於權曰：「夫中庶子官最親密，切問近對，宜用儁德。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen said to Sun Quan, "Among the offices, none is more intimate than the Household Grandee for All Purposes; for pressing questions and answers close at hand, one should employ men of outstanding virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen urged Sun Quan: "The Household Grandee for All Purposes stands closest to the heir; whoever holds it must field sharp questions at his side, so the post calls for men of real moral weight."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃用表等爲中庶子。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Chen Biao and others were appointed Household Grandees for All Purposes.
translations.idiomatic: On that advice Chen Biao and others were named Household Grandees for All Purposes.

sentences.zh: 後又以庶子禮拘，復令整巾侍坐。

translations.literal: Later, because the etiquette for grandees was restrictive, he again ordered them to straighten their headcloths and attend seated.
translations.idiomatic: Later, finding the grandees’ ritual too stiff, he had them dress their caps properly and sit with him in a more relaxed audience.

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年，權稱尊號，登爲皇太子，以恪爲左輔，休右弼，譚爲輔正，表爲翼正都尉，是爲四友，而謝景、范慎、刁玄、羊衜等皆爲賔客，

translations.literal: In the first year of Huanglong, when Sun Quan assumed the imperial title, Deng became imperial heir apparent. Ke was made Left Support, Xiu Right Support, Tan Rectifier, and Biao Chief Commandant for Wing Rectification—these were the Four Friends—while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others all served as guests.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Huanglong year Sun Quan took the throne; Sun Deng was named imperial heir. Zhuge Ke became Left Support, Zhang Xiu Right Support, Gu Tan Rectifier of the Heir, Chen Biao Chief Commandant for Wing Rectification—the “Four Friends”—and Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others joined the heir’s circle as guests.

sentences.zh: 〈衜音道。〉

translations.literal: 〈Dao is read dao.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The gloss reads the character written Dao with the same pronunciation as the common graph for 'way.'〉

sentences.zh: 於是東宮號爲多士。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Palace was said to abound in gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: From then on people said the heir’s quarters were crowded with talent.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：慎字孝敬，廣陵人，竭忠知己之君，纏綿三益之友，時人榮之。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Shen, courtesy name Xiaojing, was a man from Guangling; he devoted himself to rulers who knew him and clung to friends who improved him in three ways, and people of the time honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu lu says Fan Shen, courtesy name Xiaojing, came from Guangling; he gave himself wholly to a lord who truly knew him and to friends who sharpened him on three fronts, and contemporaries thought that distinction enviable.

sentences.zh: 著論二十篇，名曰《矯非》。

translations.literal: He composed twenty essays under the title Jiao fei ("Correcting what is wrong").
translations.idiomatic: He wrote twenty treatises collected as Correcting Error.

sentences.zh: 後爲侍中，出補武昌左部督，治軍整頓。

translations.literal: Later he became Palace Attendant, then went out to fill the post of Left Commander of Wuchang, where he put the army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant, then was posted out as Left Commander at Wuchang and ran the garrison with notable discipline.

sentences.zh: 孫皓移都，甚憚之，詔曰：「慎勳德俱茂，朕所敬憑，宜登上公，以副衆望。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao moved the capital, he greatly feared Shen and issued an edict saying, "Shen's merit and virtue are both abundant; he is one on whom I rely and whom I respect. He should be promoted to the highest noble rank to answer the expectations of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Hao shifted the capital he grew wary of Fan Shen and issued an edict praising his “abundant merit and virtue,” calling him a pillar of the throne, and saying he should be raised to the highest rank to satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 」以爲太尉。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen was named Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 慎自恨久爲將，遂託老耄。

translations.literal: Shen bitterly regretted having long served as a general and therefore pleaded extreme old age.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen, bitter that he had spent his life in uniform, pleaded senility.

sentences.zh: 軍士戀之，舉營爲之隕涕。

translations.literal: The soldiers loved him; the whole camp wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: The troops loved him; the entire camp wept when he left.

sentences.zh: 鳳凰三年卒，子耀嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Fenghuang; his son Yao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third Fenghuang year; his son Fan Yao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 玄，丹楊人。

translations.literal: Xuan was a man from Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xuan was from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 衜，南陽人。

translations.literal: Dao was a man from Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 《吳書》曰：衜初爲中庶子，年二十。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Dao first served as Household Grandee for All Purposes at the age of twenty.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu shu records that Yang Dao first held the post of Household Grandee for All Purposes at twenty.

sentences.zh: 時廷尉監隱蕃交結豪傑，自衞將軍全琮等皆傾心敬待，惟衜及宣詔郎豫章楊迪拒絕不與通，時人咸怪之。

translations.literal: At that time the Court Supervisor Yin Fan was courting connection with bold spirits; from Guard General Quan Zong downward all inclined their hearts and treated him with respect, only Dao and the Edict Clerk Yang Di of Yuzhang refused to associate with him, and people of the time all thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Court Supervisor Yin Fan was networking with local powerbrokers, and even Guard General Quan Zong courted him—only Yang Dao and the Edict Clerk Yang Di of Yuzhang would have nothing to do with Yin, which contemporaries found odd.

sentences.zh: 而蕃後叛逆，衆乃服之。

translations.literal: Later Fan rebelled, and then the crowd acknowledged their judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Fan later turned traitor, everyone conceded that Yang Dao and Yang Di had been right.

sentences.zh: 《江表傳》曰：登使侍中胡綜作賔友目曰：「英才卓越，超踰倫匹，則諸葛恪。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Deng had Palace Attendant Hu Zong compose a "catalog of guest companions," saying, "For surpassing talent that towers above its peers, there is Zhuge Ke.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang biao zhuan says Sun Deng had Palace Attendant Hu Zong draft appraisals of his companions: “For brilliance that outstrips the common run, there is Zhuge Ke.”

sentences.zh: 精識時機，達幽究微，則顧譚。

translations.literal: For keen insight into the moment, plumbing the subtle and investigating the hidden, there is Gu Tan.
translations.idiomatic: “For reading the times and sounding the depths, there is Gu Tan.”

sentences.zh: 凝辨宏達，言能釋結，則謝景。

translations.literal: For concentrated judgment, broad penetration, and speech that can untie knots, there is Xie Jing.
translations.idiomatic: “For poised judgment, wide grasp, and words that cut through tangles, there is Xie Jing.”

sentences.zh: 究學甄微，游夏同科，則范慎。

translations.literal: For exhaustive study and discriminating the subtle, ranking with You and Xia, there is Fan Shen.
translations.idiomatic: “For scholarship that sifts the fine points and matches the disciples You and Xia, there is Fan Shen.”

sentences.zh: 」衜乃私駁綜曰：「元遜才而疏，子嘿精而狠，叔發辯而浮，孝敬深而狹。

translations.literal: " Dao privately refuted Zong, saying, "Yuansun has talent but is careless; Zimo is keen but cruel; Shufa is eloquent but shallow; Xiaojing is deep but narrow."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao quietly contradicted Hu Zong: “Yuansun is gifted but careless; Zimo is sharp but ruthless; Shufa is quick-tongued but shallow; Xiaojing is thoughtful but cramped.”

sentences.zh: 」所言皆有指趣。

translations.literal: What he said had point in every case.
translations.idiomatic: Each verdict hit a nerve.

sentences.zh: 而衜卒以此言見咎，不爲恪等所親。

translations.literal: Yet Dao was blamed for these words and was not drawn close by Ke and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He was resented for those remarks and never became intimate with Zhuge Ke’s clique.

sentences.zh: 後四人皆敗，吳人謂衜之言有徵。

translations.literal: Later all four men met ruin, and the people of Wu said Dao's words had been borne out.
translations.idiomatic: When all four later fell, Wu opinion decided that Yang Dao had seen them clearly.

sentences.zh: 位至桂陽太守，卒。〉

translations.literal: He rose to the rank of Administrator of Guiyang and died.〉
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Guiyang and died.〉

sentences.zh: 權遷都建業，徵上大將軍陸遜輔登鎮武昌，領宮府留事。

translations.literal: Sun Quan moved the capital to Jianye and summoned Senior General Lu Xun to assist Deng in guarding Wuchang, in charge of the heir's establishment and capital affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan transferred the seat of government to Jianye and called Lu Xun north to steady Sun Deng at Wuchang, leaving him in charge of the heir’s household and everything that stayed behind at the old capital.

sentences.zh: 登或射獵，當由徑道，常遠避良田，不踐苗稼，至所頓息，又擇空閑之地，其不欲煩民如此。

translations.literal: Sometimes when Deng went hunting, he would take bypaths, always keeping far from good fields and not treading on seedling crops; when he halted to rest, he again chose empty, unused ground—such was his unwillingness to trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: On hunts he kept to side tracks, gave wide berth to farmers’ fields, and never trampled the crops; when he camped he picked bare ground so commoners would not be put out—he was that careful of the realm’s labor.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘馬出，有彈丸過，左右求之。

translations.literal: Once when he was riding out, a pellet flew past; his attendants searched for the shooter.
translations.idiomatic: Once a sling bullet whistled past his horse while he was out riding, and his escort wanted to hunt down whoever had fired it.

sentences.zh: 有一人操彈佩丸，咸以爲是，辭對不服，從者欲捶之，登不聽，使求過丸，比之非類，乃見釋。

translations.literal: There was a man carrying a sling and wearing pellets; all thought it was he. He denied it under questioning; his followers wished to beat him, but Deng did not permit it. He had them seek the pellet that had passed by, compared it, and it was not of the same kind, and only then was the man released.
translations.idiomatic: They seized a passerby with a sling and shot; everyone assumed he was guilty, but he protested his innocence. Sun Deng forbade a beating, had the actual pellet recovered, and proved it did not match the man’s ammunition, so they let him go.

sentences.zh: 又失盛水金馬盂，覺得其主，左右所爲，不忍致罰，呼責數之，長遣歸家，勑親近勿言。

translations.literal: Again he lost a golden horse-shaped water vessel; he realized who the owner was among those close to him, but could not bear to impose punishment. He called the man in, rebuked him verbally several times, sent him home for good forever, and ordered those near him not to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When a gold horse-head water bowl went missing, he knew which attendant had taken it yet could not bring himself to punish the thief: he summoned him, scolded him, dismissed him for good, and told his intimates to keep silent.

sentences.zh: 後弟慮卒，權爲之降損，登晝夜兼行，到賴鄉，自聞，即時召見。

translations.literal: Later when his younger brother Lu died, Sun Quan for his sake curtailed his pleasures; Deng traveled day and night, reached Lai Township, reported himself on his own initiative, and was summoned for an audience at once.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Sun Lu died, Sun Quan went into mourning and curtailed court life; Sun Deng raced day and night to Lai Township, announced himself, and was admitted at once.

sentences.zh: 見權悲泣，因諫曰：「慮寢疾不起，此乃命也。

translations.literal: Seeing Sun Quan weeping, he remonstrated, saying, "Lu lay ill and did not recover; this is fate.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his father in tears, he urged him: “Sun Lu’s illness ran its course—that is heaven’s decree.”

sentences.zh: 方今朔土未一，四海喁喁，天戴陛下，而以下流之念，減損大官殽饌，過於禮制，臣竊憂惶。

translations.literal: The northern heartland is not yet one; within the four seas all look upward; Heaven crowns Your Majesty—yet because of thoughts downstream, you have reduced the great kitchen's viands beyond what ritual allows; your servant secretly trembles with anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: “The north is still unconquered; the world watches you alone. Yet grief has cut your palace meals below what ritual allows—I fear for what that signals.”

sentences.zh: 」權納其言，爲之加膳。

translations.literal: " Sun Quan accepted his words and increased the meals.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan took the point and ordered richer fare again.

sentences.zh: 住十餘日，欲遣西還，深自陳乞，以乆離定省，子道有闕，又陳陸遜忠勤，無所顧憂，權遂留焉。

translations.literal: He stayed more than ten days and wished to send him back west; Deng earnestly pleaded at length that, having long been separated from attending his parents, he was deficient in the way of a son, and further stated that Lu Xun was loyal and diligent and there was nothing to worry about—whereupon Sun Quan kept him.
translations.idiomatic: After a fortnight Sun Quan meant to send him back to Wuchang, but Sun Deng begged to stay: he had missed too many days of filial duty, he said, and Lu Xun was loyal enough to hold the west without him—so Sun Quan let him remain.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，權征新城，使登居守，總知留事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe, when Sun Quan campaigned against Xincheng, he had Deng remain to guard the capital and take overall charge of affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Jiahe year Sun Quan marched on Xincheng and left Sun Deng to mind the capital and every rear-area decision.

sentences.zh: 時年穀不豐，頗有盜賊，乃表定科令，所以防禦，甚得止姦之要。

translations.literal: That year the grain harvest was not abundant and there were quite a few bandits; he therefore memorialized to fix statutes and ordinances for defense, and he grasped the essentials of stopping villainy very well.
translations.idiomatic: Grain was short and bandits active, so he drafted statutes for home defense that struck exactly at the roots of lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 初，登所生庶賤，徐夫人少有母養之恩，後徐氏以妬廢處吳，而步夫人最寵。

translations.literal: At first Deng had been born of a lowborn concubine; Lady Xu had given him a little of a mother's nurturing. Later Lady Xu was cast aside for jealousy and dwelt at Wu, while Lady Bu was most favored.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng’s birth mother had been a humble concubine, but Lady Xu had raised him for a time; later Lady Xu was deposed for jealousy and sent to Wu, while Lady Bu became Sun Quan’s favorite.

sentences.zh: 步氏有賜，登不敢辭，拜受而已。

translations.literal: When the Bu clan sent gifts, Deng did not dare refuse but bowed acceptance and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Bu’s people sent presents he accepted with a bow and never made more of it.

sentences.zh: 徐氏使至，所賜衣服，必沐浴服之。

translations.literal: When Lady Xu's messenger arrived, for the clothing she granted he invariably bathed before donning it.
translations.idiomatic: If Lady Xu sent clothing, he bathed before he put it on.

sentences.zh: 登將拜太子，辭曰：「本立而道生，欲立太子，宜先立后。

translations.literal: When Deng was about to be invested as heir apparent, he declined, saying, "When the root is established, the Way arises; if you wish to establish the heir apparent, you should first establish the empress."
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to name him crown prince, he objected: “The root must be set before the Way grows—if you mean to install an heir, establish the empress first.”

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「卿母安在？

translations.literal: " Sun Quan said, "Where is your mother?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked, “Where is your mother?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「在吳。

translations.literal: " He replied, "At Wu."
translations.idiomatic: “In Wu,” Sun Deng answered.

sentences.zh: 」權嘿然。

translations.literal: " Sun Quan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said nothing.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：弟和有寵於權，登親敬，待之如兄，常有欲讓之心。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: His younger brother He won Sun Quan's favor; Deng treated him with intimate respect like an elder brother and often had a mind to yield the position to him.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu adds that he honored his younger brother Sun He as an elder brother would and more than once thought of yielding precedence to him.〉

sentences.zh: 立凡二十一年，年三十三卒。

translations.literal: He was established for twenty-one years in all and died at the age of thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He held the position of heir for twenty-one years and died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 臨終，上疏曰：「臣以無狀，嬰抱篤疾，自省微劣，懼卒隕斃。

translations.literal: At the end he submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant, lacking good deportment, has been wrapped in grave illness; examining himself, he is mean and weak and fears he will suddenly perish.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he sent up a memorial: “I have behaved poorly and now lie under a heavy sickness; I know I am slight and fear I may fall at any moment.”

sentences.zh: 臣不自惜，念當委離供養，埋胔后土，長不復奉望宮省，朝覲日月，生無益於國，死貽陛下重慼，以此爲哽結耳。

translations.literal: Your servant does not pity himself, but thinks that he will cast off nurture and be buried in the rear earth, never again to look upon the palace precincts or behold the sun and moon in court; alive he was of no benefit to the state, and dead he will leave Your Majesty added grief—on this his throat is blocked."
translations.idiomatic: “I do not pity myself, only that I must leave your service, be laid in the earth, and never again attend your dawn and dusk levees—useless in life, I will add another wound in death.”

sentences.zh: 臣聞死生有命，長短自天，周晉、顏回有上智之才，而尚夭折，況臣愚陋，年過其壽，生爲國嗣，沒享榮祚，於臣已多，亦何悲恨哉！

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that life and death have their allotment and length and shortness lie with Heaven; the Zhou Prince Jin and Yan Hui had supreme intelligence yet still died young—how much more your servant, stupid and shallow, who has passed his span of years! Living he was heir to the state; dead he will enjoy honored fortune—for your servant it is already much; what grief or resentment can there be!
translations.idiomatic: “I know fate fixes life and span; princes Jin and Yan Hui were prodigies yet died young—how much more a dull man who has already outlived his share? I was heir to Wu in life and will take honor with me in death; I have had more than I deserve and bear no grudge.”

sentences.zh: 方今大事未定，逋寇未討，萬國喁喁，係命陛下，危者望安，亂者仰治。

translations.literal: At present the great enterprise is not settled; the fleeing bandits are not yet punished; within the myriad regions all look upward; their lives hang on Your Majesty—those in peril hope for safety; those in disorder look up to order.
translations.idiomatic: “The great work is unfinished, the enemy still in the field, and every district hangs on you—people in danger want peace; people in chaos want order.”

sentences.zh: 願陛下棄忘臣身，割下流之恩，脩黃老之術，篤養神光，加羞珍膳，廣開神明之慮，以定無窮之業，則率土幸賴，臣死無恨也。

translations.literal: " I beg Your Majesty to cast away thoughts of your servant, cut off the favors of downstream grief, cultivate the arts of Huang and Lao, earnestly nurture the divine brightness, add fine delicacies to your diet, broaden the concerns of your enlightened mind, and settle the enterprise without end—then within the bounds of the earth all will rely on your blessing, and your servant will die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: “Forget me, set grief aside, nourish yourself as the Yellow Emperor’s school advises, take richer food, widen your counsel, and secure the dynasty’s future—then though I die I die content.”

sentences.zh: 皇子和仁孝聦哲，德行清茂，宜早建置，以繫民望。

translations.literal: The imperial sons He is humane, filial, wise, and perspicacious; his virtue is clear and abundant; he should be early established to tie the hopes of the people.
translations.idiomatic: “Prince He is humane, filial, and quick-witted, with clear virtue—name him heir soon so the people have something to hold to.”

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪才略博達，器任佐時。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke's talent and strategy are broad and penetrating; his capacity fits assisting the age.
translations.idiomatic: “Zhuge Ke’s grasp of policy is wide and deep—keep him at the center of affairs.”

sentences.zh: 張休、顧譚、謝景，皆通敏有識斷，入宜委腹心，出可爲爪牙。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and Xie Jing are all penetrating and quick, with power of judgment; within they may be trusted as heart and belly, without they can serve as claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: “Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and Xie Jing are sharp judges—use them inside as confidants and outside as blades.”

sentences.zh: 范慎、華融矯矯壯節，有國士之風。

translations.literal: Fan Shen and Hua Rong are stern in stalwart integrity and have the bearing of men of the state.
translations.idiomatic: “Fan Shen and Hua Rong are iron in integrity—true ‘state knights.’”

sentences.zh: 羊衜辯捷，有專對之材。

translations.literal: Yang Dao is quick in debate and has the talent for exclusive embassies.
translations.idiomatic: “Yang Dao is quick on his feet in debate—send him when words must carry the day.”

sentences.zh: 刁玄優弘，志履道真。

translations.literal: Diao Xuan is generous and amplifying; his aims and conduct pursue the true Way.
translations.idiomatic: “Diao Xuan is broad-minded and steady—his life matches his principles.”

sentences.zh: 裴欽博記，翰采足用。

translations.literal: Pei Qin has wide memorization and literary talent sufficient for employment.
translations.idiomatic: “Pei Qin’s memory and brush are equal to any task you give him.”

sentences.zh: 蔣脩、虞翻，志節分明。

translations.literal: Jiang Xiu and Yu Fan have clear-cut determination of mind.
translations.idiomatic: “Jiang Xiu and Yu Fan hold their integrity without blur.”

sentences.zh: 凡此諸臣，或宜廊廟，或任將帥，皆練時事，明習法令，守信固義，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: All these ministers, some fit for the hall and some for command, are practiced in current affairs, clearly versed in statutes and ordinances, keep faith and hold to righteousness, and have wills that cannot be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: “Each man here belongs either in the council chamber or in the field; all know the times, the code, and unbreakable loyalty.”

sentences.zh: 此皆陛下日月所照，選置臣宮，得與從事，備知情素，敢以陳聞。

translations.literal: These are all men whom Your Majesty's sun and moon illumine; they were chosen and placed in your servant's palace, and your servant has been able to work with them and fully knows their dispositions—therefore he dares to set them forth.
translations.idiomatic: “You lit their careers yourself; I have watched them at my side and can vouch for them.”

sentences.zh: 臣重惟當今方外多虞，師旅未休，當厲六軍，以圖進取。

translations.literal: Your servant further reflects that at present beyond the borders there are many troubles and the armies have not ceased; one should rouse the six armies to plan advance.
translations.idiomatic: “Beyond the passes trouble still boils; keep the hosts ready for the next advance.”

sentences.zh: 軍以人爲衆，衆以財爲寶，竊聞郡縣頗有荒殘，民物凋弊，姦亂萌生，是以法令繁滋，刑辟重切。

translations.literal: An army takes men as its multitude; the multitude takes wealth as its treasure. Your servant has heard that commanderies and counties are in many places wasted and ruined, the people and things withered and exhausted, and treachery and disorder sprouting—therefore statutes and ordinances multiply and punishments are heavy and keen.
translations.idiomatic: “Armies live on men and men on wealth—yet I hear counties are ruined, folk exhausted, and crime spreading, which is why law piles on law and punishments bite harder.”

sentences.zh: 臣聞爲政聽民，律令與時推移，誠宜與將相大臣詳擇時宜，博采衆議，寬刑輕賦，均息力役，以順民望。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in governing one listens to the people; statutes and ordinances should shift with the times—it is truly fitting to deliberate in detail with generals and ministers on what suits the hour, broadly gather many opinions, lighten punishments and reduce levies, and equalize and rest corvée labor to comply with the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: “Good rule bends to the people’s need—widen consultation, lighten tax and labor, and move the code with the times.”

sentences.zh: 陸遜忠勤於時，出身憂國，謇謇在公，有匪躬之節。

translations.literal: Lu Xun is loyal and diligent for the times; he came forth from his person in worry for the state; he is outspoken for the public good and has the integrity of not sparing himself.
translations.idiomatic: “Lu Xun gives himself wholly to the realm—frank, selfless, the backbone of your government.”

sentences.zh: 諸葛瑾、步隲、朱然、全琮、朱據、呂岱、吾粲、闞澤、嚴畯、張承、孫怡忠於爲國，通達治體。

translations.literal: Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Quan Zong, Zhu Ju, Lü Dai, Wu Can, Kan Ze, Yan Jun, Zhang Cheng, and Sun Yi are loyal in serving the state and comprehend the substance of government.
translations.idiomatic: “Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Quan Zong, Zhu Ju, Lü Dai, Wu Can, Kan Ze, Yan Jun, Zhang Cheng, and Sun Yi are loyal servants who understand how rule actually works.”

sentences.zh: 可令陳上便宜，蠲除苛煩，愛養士馬，撫循百姓。

translations.literal: They may be ordered to memorialize on what is advantageous, abolish oppressive vexations, cherish and nurture soldiers and horses, and comfort and soothe the common people.
translations.idiomatic: “Charge them to report what helps the people—scrap petty exactions, tend the armies, soothe the districts.”

sentences.zh: 五年之外，十年之內，遠者歸復，近者盡力，兵不血刃，而大事可定也。

translations.literal: Within five years and within ten years, those far will return and submit and those near will exert their strength to the utmost; without blooding blades the great affair can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: “Given five years, perhaps ten, exiles will drift home, neighbors will bend to the plow, and you can finish the great work without another slaughter.”

sentences.zh: 臣聞『鳥之將死其鳴也哀，人之將死其言也善』，故子囊臨終，遺言戒時，君子以爲忠，豈況臣登，其能已乎？

translations.literal: Your servant has heard, "When a bird is about to die, its cry is mournful; when a man is about to die, his words are good." Therefore when Zi-nang faced the end, he left words warning the time, and the gentleman deemed him loyal—how much more your servant Deng—can he stop himself?
translations.idiomatic: “They say a dying bird’s cry is sad and a dying man’s words are true—Zi-nang’s last counsel was called loyal; how can I fall silent?”

sentences.zh: 願陛下留意聽采，臣雖死之日，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: " I beg Your Majesty to give heed and accept them; though your servant may be on the day of death, it is as the years of life.
translations.idiomatic: “Listen, I beg you—if you take this advice, my death will feel like life.”

sentences.zh: 」旣絕而後書聞，權益以摧感，言則隕涕。

translations.literal: " After his breath ceased, the letter was heard; Sun Quan was all the more crushed and moved, and when he spoke of it tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial arrived only after he had died; Sun Quan broke when he read it and wept whenever he spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 是歲，赤烏四年也。

translations.literal: That year was the fourth year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fourth Chiwu year.

sentences.zh: 謝景時爲豫章太守，不勝哀情，棄官奔赴，拜表自劾。

translations.literal: Xie Jing was at that time Administrator of Yuzhang; unable to master his grief, he cast aside office and hurried to the funeral, submitted a memorial impeaching himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jing was prefect of Yuzhang; overwhelmed, he threw down his seal and raced to the mourning hall, then memorialized to impeach himself.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「君與太子從事，異於他吏。

translations.literal: Sun Quan said, "Your association with the Heir Apparent differs from that of other officials."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan answered, “Your service to the heir was not the same as other clerks’.”

sentences.zh: 」使中使慰勞，聽復本職，發遣還郡。

translations.literal: " He sent an inner envoy to console him, permitted him to resume his original post, and sent him back to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a chamberlain to comfort Xie Jing, let him return to his post, and sent him back to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 謚登曰宣太子。

translations.literal: His posthumous name for Deng was Heir Apparent Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng was given the posthumous title “Heir Apparent Xuan.”

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：初葬句容，置園邑，奉守如法，後三年改葬蔣陵。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: At first he was buried at Jurong with a park settlement established and guardians appointed according to law; after three years he was reburied at Jiangling.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu notes he was first buried at Jurong with a full funerary estate, then moved three years later to the imperial tombs at Jiangling.〉

sentences.zh: 子璠、希，皆早卒，次子英，封吳侯。

translations.literal: His sons Fan and Xi both died early; the second son, Ying, was enfeoffed Marquis of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Sun Fan and Sun Xi died young; the second son, Sun Ying, was made marquis of Wu.

sentences.zh: 五鳳元年，英以大將軍孫峻擅權，謀誅峻，事覺自殺，國除。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wufeng, Ying, because Grand General Sun Jun monopolized power, plotted to execute Jun; when the affair was discovered he killed himself, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Wufeng year Sun Ying tried to kill regent Sun Jun for usurping authority; the plot leaked and Sun Ying took his own life, and his fief was struck off.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：孫和以無罪見殺，衆庶皆懷憤歎，前司馬桓慮因此招合將吏，欲共殺峻立英，事覺，皆見殺，英實不知。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu li states: When Sun He was killed though without guilt, the common people all harbored indignant sighs; the former Major Huan Lu therefore assembled generals and clerks wishing together to kill Jun and establish Ying; when the affair was discovered, all were killed, and Ying truly did not know of it.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu li claims the people mourned the innocent Sun He, that the former major Huan Lu then gathered officers to murder Sun Jun and enthrone Sun Ying, that the plot was exposed and everyone executed, and that Sun Ying knew nothing of it.〉

sentences.zh: 謝景者字叔發，南陽宛人。

translations.literal: Xie Jing, courtesy name Shufa, was a man of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jing, courtesy name Shufa, came from Wan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 在郡有治迹，吏民稱之，以爲前有顧劭，其次即景。

translations.literal: In the commandery he had traces of good government; clerks and common people praised him, thinking that before him there had been Gu Shao and next came Jing.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he left a record of honest rule; officials and commoners ranked him just below the celebrated Gu Shao.

sentences.zh: 數年卒官。

translations.literal: After several years he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office a few years later.

sentences.zh: 孫慮字子智，登弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Lu, courtesy name Zizhi, was Deng's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lu, courtesy name Zizhi, was Sun Deng’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少敏惠有才藝，權器愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick, clever, and had talent and arts; Sun Quan valued and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and accomplished as a boy, he became Sun Quan’s favorite.

sentences.zh: 黃武七年，封建昌侯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangwu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 7 he was made marquis of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 後二年，丞相雍等奏慮性聦體達，所尚日新，比方近漢，宜進爵稱王，權未許。

translations.literal: Two years later Chancellor Yong and others memorialized that Lu's nature was intelligent, his person comprehending, what he esteemed daily renewed, and comparing him to recent Han precedent, it was fitting to advance his rank and title him king; Sun Quan did not yet grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, Chancellor Zhang Yong and colleagues urged that Sun Lu’s quick mind and balanced judgment set a new standard, that Han precedent called for a princely title, and Sun Quan—for the moment—refused.

sentences.zh: 乆之，尚書僕射存上疏曰：「帝王之興，莫不襃崇至親，以光羣后，故魯衞於周，寵冠諸侯，高帝五王，封列于漢，所以藩屏本朝，爲國鎮衞。

translations.literal: After a long while, the Vice Director of the Secretariat, Cun, submitted a memorial saying, "In the rise of emperors and kings there has been none who did not exalt the utmost kin to bring glory to the host of lords; therefore Lu and Wei under the Zhou had favor surpassing the feudatories, and the five kings of the High Emperor were enfeoffed in rows in Han—by this they screened the root court and acted as bulwarks for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Time passed, and a vice director of the Secretariat surnamed Cun (the text preserves only this fragment of his name) memorialized: “Every dynasty exalts close kin so the peerage shines—Lu and Wei under Zhou and Gaozu’s five princes in Han were the shields of the throne.”

sentences.zh: 建昌侯慮稟性聦敏，才兼文武，於古典制，宜正名號。

translations.literal: Marquis of Jianchang Lu is endowed by nature with quick intelligence, his talent spanning civil and military; according to the models of antiquity and the regulations, it is fitting to rectify his title and style.
translations.idiomatic: “Sun Lu of Jianchang is clever by nature and master of both pen and sword; classical precedent says his title should be regularized.”

sentences.zh: 陛下謙光，未肯如舊，羣寮大小，咸用於邑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty shows modest forbearance and has not been willing to act according to precedent; great and small among the host of officials are all downcast at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's humility keeps you from following established honors, and every rank at court is sunk in gloom.

sentences.zh: 方今姦寇恣睢，金鼓未弭，腹心爪牙，惟親與賢。

translations.literal: At present wicked bandits swagger unchecked; the drums of war are not yet stilled; belly, heart, claws, and fangs depend on kin and worthies alone.
translations.idiomatic: “Rebels still swagger; drums have not quieted—heart, claw, and fang must be kin and worthy men.”

sentences.zh: 輒與丞相雍等議，咸以慮宜爲鎮軍大將軍，授任偏方，以光大業。

translations.literal: Therefore I have deliberated with Chancellor Yong and others; all agree that Lu should be made General Who Guards the Army, entrusted with a side quarter, to enlarge the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: “Zhang Yong and I agree: make him General Who Guards the Army and give him a flank command to magnify the great work.”

sentences.zh: 」權乃許之，於是假節開府，治半州。

translations.literal: Sun Quan thereupon granted it; thus he was lent credentials of authority, opened a general's headquarters, and governed "half the province."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan relented: Sun Lu received the credential-axe, opened his own command, and took charge of half the lower Yangzi circuit.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》載權詔曰：「期運擾亂，凶邪肆虐，威罰有序，干戈不戢。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu records Sun Quan's edict: "The times are turbulent and evil men run wild; though awe and punishment keep order, arms have not been laid down.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu quotes an edict of Sun Quan: “Fate has turned violent and the wicked trample the realm; law still bites, yet the spears never rest.”

sentences.zh: 以慮氣志休懿，武略夙昭，必能爲國佐定大業，故授以上將之位，至以殊特之榮，寵以兵馬之勢，委以偏方之任。

translations.literal: Because Lu's spirit and resolve are fine and lofty and his martial designs have long been plain, he is sure to be able to aid the state in settling the great enterprise; therefore I invest him with a senior general's rank, extend to him extraordinary honor, favor him with the host of arms and horses, and entrust him with command of a frontier sector."
translations.idiomatic: “Sun Lu’s temper is steady, his strategy proven—he can anchor our great work—so I give him a field marshal’s table, singular honors, real troops, and a border command.”

sentences.zh: 外欲威振敵虜，厭難萬里，內欲鎮撫遠近，慰卹將士，誠慮建功立事竭命之秋也。

translations.literal: "Externally I desire to make might shake the enemy and crush trouble ten thousand li away; internally I desire to quiet near and far and comfort officers and men—truly I expect Lu, in the season when merit is forged and careers are staked on a single throw, to give his all."
translations.idiomatic: “I want him to overawe the foe beyond the passes and steady the army within—this is the hour to build a name or spend a life trying.”

sentences.zh: 慮其內脩文德，外經武訓，持盈若沖，則滿而不溢。

translations.literal: "Let him cultivate civil virtue within and drill martial discipline without; holding fullness as if it were emptiness, he may be full yet never spill over."
translations.idiomatic: “Let him polish civil rule at home and harden the camps abroad; stay humble though exalted, and he will rise without overflowing.”

sentences.zh: 敬慎乃心，無忝所受。」〉

translations.literal: "Revere and watch your heart; do not shame what you receive."〉
translations.idiomatic: “Guard your charge with care and never disgrace the trust.”〉

sentences.zh: 慮以皇子之尊，富於春秋，遠近嫌其不能留意。

translations.literal: Because Lu held the dignity of an imperial son and was still in the flush of youth, those near and far suspected he would not be able to keep his mind on duty.
translations.idiomatic: People worried that a prince so young would lose focus on real work.

sentences.zh: 及至臨事，遵奉法度，敬納師友，過於衆望。

translations.literal: When it came to handling affairs, he obeyed the law, respectfully accepted teachers and companions, and exceeded what the crowd had hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took office he followed every statute, listened to his tutors, and outran every expectation.

sentences.zh: 年二十，嘉禾元年卒。

translations.literal: At age twenty he died in the first year of Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiahe 1 at twenty.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Without an heir, his marquisate was struck off.

sentences.zh: 孫和字子孝，慮弟也。

translations.literal: Sun He, courtesy name Zixiao, was Lu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He, whose courtesy name was Zixiao, was Sun Lu’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少以母王有寵見愛，年十四，爲置宮衞，使中書令闞澤教以書藝。

translations.literal: In youth, because his mother Lady Wang enjoyed favor, he was doted on; at fourteen, palace guards were established for him, and Prefect of the Masters of Writing Kan Ze was ordered to teach him writing and the arts.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Wang’s favor won him Sun Quan’s affection; at fourteen he received a household guard and Kan Ze, as director of the secretariat, tutored him in letters.

sentences.zh: 好學下士，甚見稱述。

translations.literal: He loved learning and humbled himself before gentlemen, and was much praised.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books, treated scholars with deference, and earned wide praise.

sentences.zh: 赤烏五年，立爲太子，時年十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chiwu he was established as heir apparent, at the age of nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwu 5 made him crown prince; he was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 闞澤爲太傅，薛綜爲少傅，而蔡穎、張純、封俌、嚴維等皆從容侍從。

translations.literal: Kan Ze became Grand Tutor, Xue Zong Junior Tutor, while Cai Ying, Zhang Chun, Feng Fu, Yan Wei, and others all attended him in easy companionship.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ze took the grand tutorship, Xue Zong the junior post, and Cai Ying, Zhang Chun, Feng Fu, Yan Wei, and others formed his informal retinue.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：和少岐嶷有智意，故權尤愛幸，常在左右，衣服禮秩雕玩珍異之賜，諸子莫得比焉。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: From youth He was precocious and intelligent, therefore Sun Quan especially loved and favored him; he was always at his side, and in gifts of clothing, ritual precedence, carved curios, and rare treasures none of the other sons could compare.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu says he was clever as a boy, so Sun Quan kept him always at hand and showered him with dress, rank, and treasures no other son matched.

sentences.zh: 好文學，善騎射，承師涉學，精識聦敏，尊敬師傅，愛好人物。

translations.literal: He loved belles-lettres, was skilled at riding and archery, received instruction from masters and pursued learning, was keen in judgment and quick in wit, respected tutors, and loved worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at literature and horsemanship, studied under noted teachers, showed sharp judgment, honored his tutors, and cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 穎等每朝見進賀，和常降意，歡以待之。

translations.literal: Whenever Ying and the others came to court to offer congratulations, He always lowered his intent and welcomed them with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cai Ying and his circle came to congratulate him, Sun He set rank aside and greeted them warmly.

sentences.zh: 講校經義，綜察是非，及訪諮朝臣，考績行能，以知優劣，各有條貫。

translations.literal: In expounding and collating the Classics' meanings, in comprehensively examining right and wrong, and in consulting court ministers and reviewing their conduct and ability to know excellence and inferiority, he had systematic order in each case.
translations.idiomatic: He led seminars on the canon, weighed right and wrong, polled ministers on policy, and rated men’s performance with cool consistency.

sentences.zh: 後諸葛壹僞叛以誘魏將諸葛誕，權潛軍待之。

translations.literal: Later Zhuge Yi feigned defection to lure Wei general Zhuge Dan; Sun Quan secretly moved troops to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhuge Yi pretended to rebel in order to bait Zhuge Dan of Wei, while Sun Quan hid an army to spring the trap.

sentences.zh: 和以權暴露外次，又戰者凶事，常憂勞憯怛，不復會同飲食，數上諫，戒令持重，務在全勝，權還，然後敢安。

translations.literal: He, because Sun Quan was exposed in an outer camp and because warfare is an inauspicious matter, was constantly anxious and grieved, no longer joining in communal drinking and eating; several times he remonstrated upward, warning him to be steady and aim at complete victory, and only when Sun Quan returned did he dare feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: With his father camped in the field—war being an ill omen—Sun He could not bring himself to feast; he sent repeated memorials urging caution and total victory, and only when Sun Quan came home did he sleep soundly.

sentences.zh: 張純字元基，敦之子。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was the son of Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was Zhang Dun’s son.

sentences.zh: 《吳錄》曰：純少厲操行，學博才秀，切問捷對，容止可觀。

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: Chun in youth cultivated conduct, his learning was broad and his talent outstanding; he pressed questions and answered swiftly, and his bearing was worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu lu records that Zhang Chun hardened his character young, read widely, shot sharp questions and quicker answers, and carried himself impressively.

sentences.zh: 拜郎中，補廣德令，治有異績，擢爲太子輔義都尉。〉

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Palace, then supplemented as magistrate of Guangde, where his administration had unusual traces of success, and he was promoted to Chief Commandant for Supporting Righteousness of the Heir Apparent.〉
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace gentleman, then magistrate of Guangde with a distinguished record, and was pulled up to chief commandant supporting the heir.〉

sentences.zh: 是時有司頗以條書問事，和以爲姦妄之人，將因事錯意，以生禍心，不可長也，表宜絕之。

translations.literal: At that time the authorities often used written questionnaires on affairs; He thought that treacherous and false men would seize on matters to twist intent and breed a mind for disaster—this could not be allowed to grow—and memorialized that it should be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats had begun sending written interrogatories; Sun He argued that schemers would twist answers to sow disaster and asked Sun Quan to forbid the practice.

sentences.zh: 又都督劉寶白庶子丁晏，晏亦白寶，和謂晏曰：「文武在事，當能幾人，因隙構簿，圖相危害，豈有福哉？

translations.literal: Again Area Commander Liu Bao denounced Household Grandee Ding Yan to the throne, and Yan in turn denounced Bao; He said to Yan, "When civil and military men hold office, how many can there be? To seize on rifts and build dossiers, plotting mutual harm—can there be blessing in that?"
translations.idiomatic: When Area Commander Liu Bao and Household Grandee Ding Yan traded accusations, Sun He told Ding Yan, “How many able officers do we have? If you tear at each other’s files you invite ruin, not fortune.”

sentences.zh: 」遂兩釋之，使之從厚。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he released both and had them treat each other generously.
translations.idiomatic: He made them drop the charges and reconcile.

sentences.zh: 常言當世士人宜講脩術學，校習射御，以周世務，而但交游博弈以妨事業，非進取之謂。

translations.literal: He constantly said that gentlemen of the age ought to lecture on and cultivate technical learning, drill archery and charioteering to meet the needs of the age, yet they only socialized and played board games to the detriment of their undertakings—this was not what advancing and taking hold meant.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured that scholars should study useful arts and drill bow and chariot for public duty, not waste days at gaming tables.

sentences.zh: 後羣寮侍宴，言及博弈，以爲妨事費日而無益於用，勞精損思而終無所成，非所以進德脩業，積累功緒者也。

translations.literal: Later when the host of officials attended a banquet and talk turned to board games, he held that they hindered affairs, wasted days, and were of no use in practice, taxing the spirit and injuring thought yet in the end accomplishing nothing—not the way to advance virtue and cultivate undertakings or accumulate merit and threads of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At a later banquet he argued that dice and boards wasted spirit, achieved nothing, and did not build character or career.

sentences.zh: 且志士愛日惜力，君子慕其大者，高山景行，恥非其次。

translations.literal: Moreover, a man of purpose cherishes days and spares his strength; the gentleman admires what is great—"high mountains and bright conduct"—and is ashamed not to rank second.
translations.idiomatic: A man of purpose hoards time and strength; a gentleman looks to the high road and is ashamed to settle for less.

sentences.zh: 夫以天地長乆，而人居其間，有白駒過隙之喻，年齒一暮，榮華不再。

translations.literal: As heaven and earth endure long yet man dwells between them, there is the metaphor of the white colt flashing past a crack; once the years turn toward evening, glory and splendor do not return.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth roll on while man flickers past like the proverbial white colt at a crevice—age turns, and splendor does not return.

sentences.zh: 凡所患者，在於人情所不能絕，誠能絕無益之欲以奉德義之塗，棄不急之務以脩功業之基，其於名行，豈不善哉？

translations.literal: All that is to be feared lies in what human feeling cannot cut off; if one can truly cut off useless desires to tread the path of virtue and righteousness, cast aside tasks that are not urgent to cultivate the foundation of merit and enterprise—how could that not be good for name and conduct?
translations.idiomatic: The trap is appetite; cut useless craving, drop busywork, and the path to reputation opens.

sentences.zh: 夫人情猶不能無嬉娛，嬉娛之好，亦在於飲宴琴書射御之間，何必博弈，然後爲歡。

translations.literal: Moreover human feeling cannot be without amusement; the good of amusement also lies among feasts, zithers, books, archery, and charioteering—why must it be board games before there is joy?
translations.idiomatic: Men need recreation, but feasts, music, books, and riding serve as well as gambling.

sentences.zh: 乃命侍坐者八人，各著論以矯之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the eight who sat in attendance each to compose an essay to correct this.
translations.idiomatic: He told the eight companions at table each to draft an essay against gaming.

sentences.zh: 於是中庶子韋曜退而論奏，和以示賔客。

translations.literal: Thereupon Household Grandee Wei Yao withdrew and composed a memorial discussion, which He showed to his guests.
translations.idiomatic: Household Grandee Wei Yao drafted a piece for him; Sun He passed it to his circle.

sentences.zh: 時蔡穎好弈，直事在署者頗斆焉，故以此諷之。

translations.literal: At the time Cai Ying loved chess, and those on duty in the office often imitated him; therefore He used this to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ying was addicted to weiqi, and clerks copied him—Sun He meant the essays as a barb at them.

sentences.zh: 是後王夫人與全公主有隙。

translations.literal: After this Lady Wang and the Princess of Quan had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lady Wang fell out with the Princess of Quan.

sentences.zh: 權嘗寢疾，和祠祭於廟，和妃叔父張休居近廟，邀和過所居。

translations.literal: Sun Quan once lay ill with fever; He performed sacrifice in the temple, and He's consort's uncle Zhang Xiu dwelt near the temple and invited He to pass by his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan fell ill, Sun He sacrificed at the ancestral shrine; his consort’s uncle Zhang Xiu lived next door and asked him in.

sentences.zh: 全公主使人覘視，因言太子不在廟中，專就妃家計議；

translations.literal: The Princess of Quan had people spy; accordingly she said the heir was not in the temple but had gone specially to the consort's kin to plot;
translations.idiomatic: The princess of Quan set spies and reported that the heir had skipped the shrine to plot at his in-laws’.

sentences.zh: 又言王夫人見上寢疾，有喜色。

translations.literal: She further said that when Lady Wang saw the sovereign lying ill, she showed a joyful expression.
translations.idiomatic: She added that Lady Wang smiled when she heard the emperor was sick.

sentences.zh: 權由是發怒，夫人憂死，而和寵稍損，懼於廢黜。

translations.literal: Sun Quan for this reason erupted in anger; the lady died of worry, and He's favor was slightly diminished as he feared deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan raged; Lady Wang died of fright; Sun He’s favor thinned and he lived in fear of deposition.

sentences.zh: 魯王霸覬覦滋甚，陸遜、吾粲、顧譚等數陳適庶之義，理不可奪，全寄、楊笁爲魯王霸支黨，譖愬日興。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu, Ba, eyed the succession ever more greedily; Lu Xun, Wu Can, Gu Tan, and others several times set forth the principle that heir and cadet must be distinct and the principle could not be wrested away; Quan Ji and Yang Zhu became partisans of the Prince of Lu Ba, and slander and complaints rose daily.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sun Ba openly coveted the throne; Lu Xun, Wu Can, and Gu Tan insisted on the heir–cadet distinction, while Quan Ji and Yang Zhu backed Sun Ba and daily poured poison into Sun Quan’s ear.

sentences.zh: 粲遂下獄誅，譚徙交州。

translations.literal: Can thereupon went to prison and was executed; Tan was banished to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Can was jailed and killed; Gu Tan was exiled to Jiao.

sentences.zh: 權沈吟者歷年，

translations.literal: Sun Quan hesitated for years,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan hesitated for years.

sentences.zh: 〈殷基《通語》曰：初權旣立和爲太子，而封霸爲魯王，初拜猶同宮室，禮秩未分。

translations.literal: 〈Yin Ji's Tong yu states: At first, after Sun Quan had established He as heir and enfeoffed Ba as Prince of Lu, at first investiture they still shared one palace compound and ritual precedence was not divided.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yin Ji’s Tong yu says that at first Sun He and Sun Ba still lived in the same palace and their ranks were not yet split.

sentences.zh: 羣公之議，以爲太子、國王上下有序，禮秩宜異，於是分宮別僚，而隙端開矣。

translations.literal: The lords' deliberation held that heir apparent and prince of the blood ought to be ordered high and low, and ritual precedence ought to differ; thereupon separate palaces and staffs were assigned, and the crack of rift opened.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued that crown prince and royal son must differ in rank, so separate households were ordered—and the feud began.

sentences.zh: 自侍御賔客造爲二端，仇黨疑貳，滋延大臣。

translations.literal: From attendants, charioteers, and guests two factions were fashioned; hostile cliques doubted each other and spread among the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and guests split into two camps, and suspicion climbed the ladder to the great officers.

sentences.zh: 丞相陸遜、大將軍諸葛恪、太常顧譚、驃騎將軍朱據、會稽太守滕胤、大都督施績、尚書丁密等奉禮而行，宗事太子，驃騎將軍步隲、鎮南將軍呂岱、大司馬全琮、左將軍呂據、中書令孫弘等附魯王，中外官僚將軍大臣舉國中分。

translations.literal: Chancellor Lu Xun, Grand General Zhuge Ke, Grand Master of Ceremonies Gu Tan, Cavalry General Zhu Ju, Administrator of Kuaiji Teng Yin, Area Commander Shi Ji, Minister Ding Mi, and others observed ritual and acted, honoring the heir apparent; Cavalry General Bu Zhi, General Who Guards the South Lü Dai, Grand Marshal Quan Zong, General of the Left Lü Ju, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Sun Hong, and others attached to the Prince of Lu; inner and outer clerks, generals, and great ministers split the whole state down the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, Zhuge Ke, Gu Tan, Zhu Ju, Teng Yin, Shi Ji, Ding Mi, and others backed the heir; Bu Zhi, Lü Dai, Quan Zong, Lü Ju, Sun Hong, and others backed the Prince of Lu—court and camp were torn in two.

sentences.zh: 權患之，謂侍中孫峻曰：「子弟不睦，臣下分部，將有袁氏之敗，爲天下笑。

translations.literal: Sun Quan worried over it and said to Palace Attendant Sun Jun, "When sons and younger brothers are not harmonious and subordinates divide into factions, there will be the defeat of the Yuan clan and the world will laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told Sun Jun, “If brothers feud and officers pick sides, we repeat the Yuan disaster and become a laughingstock.”

sentences.zh: 一人立者，安得不亂？

translations.literal: " If one is established, how can there not be chaos?
translations.idiomatic: “Name one heir and how can the realm stay quiet?”

sentences.zh: 」於是有改嗣之規矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon there were plans to change the successor.
translations.idiomatic: Plans to replace the heir took shape.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以爲袁紹、劉表謂尚、琮爲賢，本有傳後之意，異於孫權旣以立和而復寵霸，坐生亂階，自構家禍，方之袁、劉，昏悖甚矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Yuan Shao and Liu Biao deemed Shang and Cong worthy and originally had intention to transmit the succession—this differs from Sun Quan, who after having established He again favored Ba, thereby sitting and producing the steps of disorder and constructing family calamity himself; compared to Yuan and Liu, he was far more muddled and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that Yuan Shao and Liu Biao truly preferred younger sons, whereas Sun Quan first installed Sun He then pampered Sun Ba—he courted the disaster himself and outdid Yuan and Liu in folly.

sentences.zh: 步隲以德度著稱，爲吳良臣，而阿附於霸，事同楊笁，何哉？

translations.literal: Bu Zhi was famed for virtue and measure and was a good minister of Wu—yet he fawned on Ba in the same affair as Yang Zhu; why?
translations.idiomatic: Bu Zhi was a statesman of reputation—why did he cling to Sun Ba like Yang Zhu?

sentences.zh: 和旣正位，適庶分定，就使才德不殊，猶將義不黨庶，況霸實無聞，而和爲令嗣乎？

translations.literal: He had already taken correct position; heir and cadet were settled; granting that talents were not different, still the right would not side with the cadet—how much more when Ba truly had no reputation and He was the lawful heir?
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir was fixed, decency forbade favoring the cadet—especially when Sun Ba had done nothing to earn the throne.

sentences.zh: 夫邪僻之人，豈其舉體無善，但一爲不善，衆美皆亡耳。

translations.literal: As for depraved men, is it that their whole persons lack good? It is only that once they do one thing not good, all their excellences perish.
translations.idiomatic: Villains are not wholly base—one bad choice erases every virtue.

sentences.zh: 隲若果有此事，則其餘不足觀矣！

translations.literal: If Zhi truly did this thing, then the rest is not worth viewing!
translations.idiomatic: If Bu Zhi really chose that faction, nothing else he did can redeem him.

sentences.zh: 呂岱、全琮之徒，蓋所不足論耳。〉

translations.literal: As for Lü Dai, Quan Zong, and their sort, they are hardly worth discussing.〉
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai and Quan Zong scarcely merit mention.〉

sentences.zh: 後遂幽閉和。

translations.literal: Later He was then confined in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He was imprisoned in isolation.

sentences.zh: 於是驃騎將軍朱據、尚書僕射屈晃率諸將吏泥頭自縛，連日詣闕請和。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cavalry General Zhu Ju and Vice Director of the Secretariat Qu Huang led various generals and clerks, mud on their heads and bonds on themselves, for days on end going to the palace gate to beg for He.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ju and Vice Director Qu Huang led officers with earth on their foreheads and ropes on their wrists to the palace gate day after day pleading for Sun He.

sentences.zh: 權登白爵觀見，甚惡之，勑據、晃等無事忩忩。

translations.literal: Sun Quan ascended the White Heron Watch and saw it, greatly detested it, and ordered Ju, Huang, and the others not to be in such frantic haste over nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan mounted the White Heron Tower, hated the sight, and barked at them to stop their clamor.

sentences.zh: 權欲廢和立亮，無難督陳正、五營督陳象上書，稱引晉獻公殺申生，立奚齊，晉國擾亂，又據、晃固諫不止。

translations.literal: Sun Quan wished to depose He and establish Liang; the Commandant Without Difficulty Chen Zheng and the Commandant of the Five Camps Chen Xiang submitted memorials, citing Duke Xian of Jin killing Shen Sheng and establishing Xi Qi and the turmoil of the state of Jin; again Ju and Huang firmly remonstrated without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to depose Sun He for Sun Liang; Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang cited Duke Xian of Jin’s murder of Crown Prince Sheng; Zhu Ju and Qu Huang still would not relent.

sentences.zh: 權大怒，族誅正、象，據、晃牽入殿，杖一百，

translations.literal: Sun Quan was greatly angry, exterminated the clans of Zheng and Xiang, had Ju and Huang dragged into the hall, and caned them one hundred strokes,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan massacred Chen Zheng’s and Chen Xiang’s families and had Zhu Ju and Qu Huang flogged a hundred strokes in court,

sentences.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：晃入，口諫曰：「太子仁明，顯聞四海。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu li states: When Huang entered, he remonstrated with his mouth, saying, "The heir apparent is humane and enlightened; his fame spreads within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu li says Qu Huang shouted from the floor that the crown prince’s virtue was known everywhere.

sentences.zh: 今三方鼎跱，實不宜搖動太子，以生衆心。

translations.literal: " Now the three sides stand like tripod legs; it is truly not fitting to shake the heir apparent and breed the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: “The three kingdoms brace like a tripod—this is no time to unsettle the heir.”

sentences.zh: 願陛下少垂聖慮，老臣雖死，猶生之年。

translations.literal: " I beg Your Majesty slightly to extend sagely consideration; though your old servant may die, it will be as the years of life.
translations.idiomatic: “Spare one thought for wisdom, and though I die I live again.”

sentences.zh: 」叩頭流血，辭氣不撓。

translations.literal: " He knocked his head until it bled; his words and tone did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: He beat his head on the stone until the blood ran but would not yield.

sentences.zh: 權不納晃言，斥還田里。

translations.literal: Sun Quan did not accept Huang's words and dismissed him to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan refused him and sent him home to farm.

sentences.zh: 孫皓即位，詔曰：「故僕射屈晃，志匡社稷，忠諫亡身。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao assumed the throne, he issued an edict saying, "The former Vice Director Qu Huang, his aim was to rectify the altars of soil and grain; with loyal remonstrance he lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao later edicted that Qu Huang had died trying to save the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 封晃子緒爲東陽亭侯，弟幹、恭爲立義都尉。

translations.literal: " He enfeoffed Huang's son Xu as village marquis of Dongyang, and younger brothers Gan and Gong as Chief Commandants for Establishing Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Qu Huang’s son Qu Xu and named his brothers commandants.

sentences.zh: 」緒後亦至尚書僕射。

translations.literal: " Xu later also reached the rank of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Xu rose to vice director of the secretariat in his turn.

sentences.zh: 晃，汝南人，見胡沖荅問。

translations.literal: Huang was a man from Runan; see Hu Chong's replies to questions.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huang came from Runan—see Hu Chong’s dialogues.

sentences.zh: 《吳書》曰：張純亦盡言極諫，權幽之，遂棄市。〉

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Zhang Chun also spoke to the utmost in remonstrance; Sun Quan confined him and then had him exposed in the market.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wu shu adds that Zhang Chun argued to the death, was jailed, then executed in the marketplace.〉

sentences.zh: 竟徙和於故鄣，羣司坐諫誅放者十數。

translations.literal: In the end He was moved to Guzhang; more than ten offices sat in remonstration and were killed or banished.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He was banished to Guzhang; a dozen officials who protested were killed or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 衆咸冤之。

translations.literal: The multitude all thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion called it a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：權寢疾，意頗感寤，欲徵和還立之，全公主及孫峻、孫弘等固爭之，乃止。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: When Sun Quan lay ill he was somewhat moved to insight and wished to summon He back and establish him; the Princess of Quan and Sun Jun, Sun Hong, and others firmly opposed it, and therefore he desisted.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu claims Sun Quan near death wanted Sun He restored but the Princess of Quan, Sun Jun, and Sun Hong blocked him.〉

sentences.zh: 孫休立，封和子皓爲烏程侯，自新都之本國。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu was established, he enfeoffed He's son Hao as marquis of Wucheng, and Hao went from Xindu to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu enthroned Sun He’s son Sun Hao as marquis of Wucheng and sent him from Xindu to his fief.

sentences.zh: 休薨，皓即阼，其年追謚父和曰文皇帝，改葬明陵，置園邑二百家，令、丞奉守。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Hao succeeded to the throne; that year he posthumously titled his father He as Emperor Wen, reburied him at Ming Mausoleum, established a park settlement of two hundred households, and ordered a magistrate and assistant to maintain the guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu died Sun Hao took the throne, posthumously named his father Emperor Wen, reburied him at Mingling with a two-hundred-household guard.

sentences.zh: 後年正月，又分吳郡、丹楊九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程，置太守，四時奉祠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, he again divided nine counties of Wu commandery and Danyang to form Wu Xing commandery, with headquarters at Wucheng, established an administrator, and performed seasonal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The next New Year he carved nine counties from Wu and Danyang into Wu Xing commandery, capital at Wucheng, with a prefect to keep the seasonal rites.

sentences.zh: 有司奏言，宜立廟京邑。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized that it was fitting to establish a temple in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats urged a shrine in the capital.

sentences.zh: 寶鼎二年七月，使守大匠薛珝營立寢堂，號曰清廟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Baoding, he sent Supervising Grand Engineer Xue Xu to build a hall of repose, styled the Pure Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding 2, seventh month: he ordered Xue Xu to raise a mortuary hall called the Pure Temple.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣守丞相孟仁、太常姚信等備官寮中軍步騎二千人，以靈輿法駕，東迎神於明陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he dispatched Acting Chancellor Meng Ren, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yao Xin, and others with the full complement of officials, two thousand foot and horse of the central army, with the spirit carriage and statutory equipage, to go east and welcome the spirit at Ming Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Meng Ren, Yao Xin, two thousand guards, and the imperial hearse went east to Mingling for the spirit.

sentences.zh: 皓引見仁，親拜送於庭。

translations.literal: Hao led Ren in to audience and personally bowed seeing him off in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao received Meng Ren in court and bowed him off in person.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：比仁還，中使手詔，日夜相繼，奉問神靈起居動止。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: By the time Ren returned, inner envoys with autograph edicts succeeded one another day and night, conveying inquiries after the spirit's rest and movements.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu says couriers with the emperor’s own brush rode day and night asking how the ghost fared.

sentences.zh: 巫覡言見和被服，顏色如平生日，皓悲喜涕淚，悉召公卿尚書詣闕門下受賜。〉

translations.literal: The shamans said they saw He in cap and robes, his complexion as on ordinary days of life; Hao was moved between joy and grief, weeping; he summoned all dukes, ministers, and Masters of Writing to the gate below the palace to receive gifts.〉
translations.idiomatic: Mediums claimed Sun He appeared in court dress as in life; Sun Hao wept, then feasted the whole high command at the gate.〉

sentences.zh: 靈輿當至，使丞相陸凱奉三牲祭於近郊，皓於金城外露宿。

translations.literal: When the spirit carriage was about to arrive, he ordered Chancellor Lu Kai to offer the three sacrificial victims in sacrifice in the near suburbs, while Hao lodged in the open outside Jin Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai sacrificed the three victims in the near suburb while Sun Hao slept in the cold outside Jin City.

sentences.zh: 明日，望拜於東門之外。

translations.literal: The next day he performed obeisance in the gaze of worship east of the outer gate.
translations.idiomatic: Next dawn he bowed toward the east beyond the gate.

sentences.zh: 其翌日，拜廟薦祭，歔欷悲感。

translations.literal: On the day following that, he bowed in the temple and presented sacrifice, sighing and moved with grief.
translations.idiomatic: The day after, he entered the temple, offered wine, and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 比七日三祭，倡技晝夜娛樂。

translations.literal: For nearly seven days he performed sacrifice thrice; singers and performers entertained day and night.
translations.idiomatic: For seven days he held three daily oblations while musicians played round the clock.

sentences.zh: 有司奏言「祭不欲數，數則黷，宜以禮斷情」，然後止。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized, "Sacrifice ought not to be frequent; frequency is irreverence; it is fitting to cut off feeling by ritual," and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers protested that too many offerings profaned the rites; he stopped only when they cited precedent.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：和四子：皓、德、謙、俊。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu li states: He had four sons: Hao, De, Qian, and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu li lists four sons: Sun Hao, Sun De, Sun Qian, Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 孫休即位，封德錢唐侯，謙永安侯，俊拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu assumed the throne, he enfeoffed De as marquis of Qiantang, Qian as marquis of Yongan, and Jun was appointed Chief Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu made Sun De marquis of Qiantang, Sun Qian marquis of Yongan, and Sun Jun cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 皓在武昌，吳興施但因民之不堪命，聚萬餘人，劫謙，將至秣陵，欲立之。

translations.literal: When Hao was at Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, because the people could not bear their orders, gathered more than ten thousand men, seized Qian, and was about to bring him to Moling intending to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: While Sun Hao ruled from Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, claiming the people were crushed, raised ten thousand men, kidnapped Sun Qian, and marched on Moling to enthrone him.

sentences.zh: 未至三十里住，擇吉日，但遣使以謙命詔丁固、諸葛靚。

translations.literal: Before they had gone thirty li they halted, chose an auspicious day, but sent an envoy in Qian's name to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li short of the capital they halted; Shi Dan used Sun Qian’s name to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.

sentences.zh: 靚即斬其使。

translations.literal: Jing thereupon beheaded his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing beheaded the messenger.

sentences.zh: 但遂前到九里，固、靚出擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Dan thereupon advanced forward to Jiuli; Gu and Jing came out and attacked, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan pushed on to Jiuli; Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing sallied and shattered him.

sentences.zh: 但兵裸身無鎧甲，臨陣皆披散。

translations.literal: Dan's soldiers were naked without armor; facing battle they all let their hair hang loose.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan’s men fought stripped to the waist without mail.

sentences.zh: 謙獨坐車中，遂生獲之。

translations.literal: Qian alone sat in a carriage and was thereupon captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian sat alone in a cart and was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 固不敢殺，以狀告皓，皓酖之，母子皆死。

translations.literal: Gu did not dare kill him but reported the situation to Hao; Hao poisoned him with ale, and mother and son both died.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gu dared not execute him and reported to Sun Hao, who poisoned Sun Qian and his mother.

sentences.zh: 俊，張承外孫，聦明辨惠，爲遠近所稱，皓又殺之。〉

translations.literal: Jun was maternal grandson of Zhang Cheng, intelligent, discriminating, and quick, praised by those far and near, and Hao again killed him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun, Zhang Cheng’s grandson, was clever and admired near and far—Sun Hao killed him too.〉

sentences.zh: 孫霸字子威，和弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Ba, courtesy name Ziwei, was He's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ba, courtesy name Ziwei, was Sun He’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 和爲太子。

translations.literal: He was heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He held the position of crown prince.

sentences.zh: 霸爲魯王，寵愛崇特，與和無殊。

translations.literal: Ba was Prince of Lu; favor, love, and elevation were lofty and special, no different from He's.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ba was Prince of Lu, yet Sun Quan showered him with the same favor he gave the heir.

sentences.zh: 頃之，和、霸不穆之聲聞於權耳，權禁斷往來，假以精學。

translations.literal: Before long the voices of discord between He and Ba reached Sun Quan's ears; Sun Quan forbade and cut off their mutual visiting, granting them the pretext of concentrated study.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word of the brothers’ feud reached Sun Quan, who barred their courts from each other and called it “dedication to scholarship.”

sentences.zh: 督軍使者羊衜上疏曰：「臣聞古之有天下者，皆先顯別適庶，封建子弟，所以尊重祖宗，爲國藩表也。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Envoy Yang Dao submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that those of old who possessed the under Heaven all first clearly distinguished heir and cadet, enfeoffing sons and younger brothers, thereby honoring the ancestors and acting as screens and markers for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao, as army supervisor envoy, wrote: “Ancient kings always drew a bright line between heir and younger sons and enfeoffed the rest, both to honor the ancestors and to fence the throne.”

sentences.zh: 二宮拜授，海內稱宜，斯乃大吳興隆之基。

translations.literal: When the two palaces received appointment, within the seas it was called fitting—this is the foundation of Great Wu's flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The dual investiture won praise across the realm as the bedrock of Wu’s strength.”

sentences.zh: 頃聞二宮並絕賔客，遠近悚然，大小失望。

translations.literal: Recently your servant has heard that both palaces have altogether cut off guests; near and far are struck with fear, great and small disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: “Now both households have shut their doors to visitors, and the whole country is uneasy.”

sentences.zh: 竊從下風，聽採衆論，咸謂二宮智達英茂，自正名建號，於今三年，德行內著，美稱外昭，西北二隅，乆所服聞。

translations.literal: Your servant, following the lower wind, has listened and gathered the many discussions; all say that the two palaces in wisdom reach excellence and splendor; from the time they corrected their names and established their styles until now three years have passed; virtue and conduct are manifest within and fair praise shines without; the two corners northwest have long submitted and heard.
translations.idiomatic: “From what I hear, both princes are bright; three years under their proper titles they have earned praise at home and respect in Wei and Shu.”

sentences.zh: 謂陛下當副順遐邇所以歸德，勤命二宮賔延四遠，使異國聞聲，思爲臣妾。

translations.literal: They say Your Majesty ought to answer the compliance of far and near whereby they return their virtue, diligently ordering the two palaces to extend guests to the four quarters, causing foreign states to hear the sound and wish to become servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: “We expected you to answer that loyalty by letting both courts again host men from every quarter so distant powers would wish to submit.”

sentences.zh: 今旣未垂意於此，而發明詔，省奪備衞，抑絕賔客，使四方禮敬，不復得通，雖實陛下敦尚古義，欲令二宮專志於學，不復顧慮觀聽小宜，期於溫故博物而已，然非臣下傾企喁喁之至願也。

translations.literal: Now, since you have not yet extended intent in this direction but have issued a clarifying edict, reducing and taking away complete guard, suppressing and cutting off guests, so that the ritual respect of the four quarters can no longer get through—though in truth Your Majesty esteems and honors ancient meanings, wishing to make the two palaces fix their minds on study and no longer heed listening to small conveniences, aiming only at reviewing the old and broadly knowing things—yet it is not the utmost hope of which your subordinates crane their necks and look upward with one voice."
translations.idiomatic: “Instead you issued an edict stripping guards and guests—perhaps to keep them at their books—but it is not what your servants hoped to see.”

sentences.zh: 或謂二宮不遵典式，此臣所以寢息不寧。

translations.literal: Some say the two palaces do not follow canonical models—this is why your servant lies down and rises without peace.
translations.idiomatic: “Rumors say both courts break precedent—that is what keeps me awake.”

sentences.zh: 就如所嫌，猶宜補察，密加斟酌，不使遠近得容異言。

translations.literal: Granting what they suspect, still one ought to investigate in supplement, secretly add deliberation, and not allow far and near to harbor different words.
translations.idiomatic: “If there is fault, investigate quietly; do not let gossip spread.”

sentences.zh: 臣懼積疑成謗，乆將宣流，而西北二隅，去國不遠，異同之語，易以聞達。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that accumulated doubt will become slander, and in time it will spread abroad; while the two corners northwest are not far from the state, words of agreement and difference easily reach hearing.
translations.idiomatic: “Suspicion curdles into slander, and the northwest borders are close enough that rumor crosses to the enemy.”

sentences.zh: 聞達之日，聲論當興，將謂二宮有不順之愆，不審陛下何以解之？

translations.literal: When the day of hearing arrives, voices and discussions will arise; they will say the two palaces have the fault of not being compliant—your servant does not examine how Your Majesty will explain it?
translations.idiomatic: “When that talk starts, men will say the princes plot treason—how will you answer Wei and Shu?”

sentences.zh: 若無以解異國，則亦無以釋境內。

translations.literal: If there is no means to explain to foreign states, then there is also no means to release doubt within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: “If you cannot convince outsiders, you cannot calm your own people.”

sentences.zh: 境內守疑，異國興謗，非所以育巍巍，鎮社稷也。

translations.literal: Doubt guarding within the borders and slander arising in foreign states are not the means to nurture loftiness and quiet the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: “Domestic doubt and foreign calumny do not nurture majesty or steady the altars.”

sentences.zh: 願陛下早發優詔，使二宮周旋禮命如初，則天清地晏，萬國幸甚矣。」

translations.literal: " I beg Your Majesty early to issue a generous edict, causing the two palaces to move in ritual command as at the beginning—then heaven will be clear and earth tranquil, and within the myriad regions there will be extreme good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: “Issue a generous edict, reopen both courts, restore the old courtesies—then heaven clears, earth rests, and the realm rejoices.”

sentences.zh: 時全寄、吳安、孫奇、楊笁等陰共附霸，圖危太子。

translations.literal: At that time Quan Ji, Wu An, Sun Qi, Yang Zhu, and others secretly together attached to Ba and plotted to endanger the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Ji, Wu An, Sun Qi, and Yang Zhu secretly backed Sun Ba against the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 譖毀旣行，太子以敗，霸亦賜死。

translations.literal: When slander and destruction had gone forward, the heir apparent thereby failed, and Ba was also ordered to die by gift.
translations.idiomatic: The smears worked: the heir fell, and Sun Ba was forced to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 流笁屍于江，兄穆以數諫戒笁，得免大辟，猶徙南州。

translations.literal: Zhu's corpse was floated in the river; his elder brother Mu, because he several times remonstrated and warned Zhu, was spared the great death penalty, but was still banished to the southern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhu’s body was cast into the Yangzi; his brother Yang Mu, who had warned him, escaped execution but was exiled south.

sentences.zh: 霸賜死後，又誅寄、安、奇等，咸以黨霸搆和故也。

translations.literal: After Ba was ordered to die by gift, Ji, An, Qi, and others were also executed—all because they had factionally attached to Ba and framed He.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Ba’s death Sun Quan executed Quan Ji, Wu An, and Sun Qi for plotting with him against Sun He.

sentences.zh: 孫奮字子揚，霸弟也，母曰仲姬。

translations.literal: Sun Fen, courtesy name Ziyang, was Ba's younger brother; his mother was called Lady Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen, courtesy name Ziyang, was Sun Ba’s brother; his mother was Lady Zhongji.

sentences.zh: 太元二年，立爲齊王，居武昌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiyuan he was established as Prince of Qi and dwelt at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan 2 made him prince of Qi with his seat at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 權薨，太傅諸葛恪不欲諸王處江濵兵馬之地，徙奮於豫章。
