translations.literal: When Sun Quan died, Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke did not wish the various kings to be at places of arms and horses along the riverbank, and moved Fen to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan’s death Zhuge Ke refused to leave princes on the Yangzi garrison line and transferred Sun Fen to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 奮怒，不從命，又數越法度。

translations.literal: Fen was angry, did not obey the order, and also repeatedly transgressed the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen refused the order and broke the rules again and again.

sentences.zh: 恪上牋諫曰：「帝王之尊，與天同位，是以家天下，臣父兄，四海之內，皆爲臣妾。

translations.literal: Ke submitted a note remonstrating: "The honor of emperor and king shares position with Heaven; therefore he makes the world his family, and fathers and elder brothers are ministers; within the four seas all are servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke wrote: “The Son of Heaven shares rank with heaven—he owns the realm and even kin are his subjects.”

sentences.zh: 仇讎有善，不得不舉，親戚有惡，不得不誅，所以承天理物，先國後身，蓋聖人立制，百代不易之道也。

translations.literal: In enemies there is good that cannot but be raised; in kin there is evil that cannot but be punished—by this he receives Heaven's principle and orders things, putting the state first and himself after; this is the way the sage kings established institutions, the Way not altered for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: “He must reward a foe’s virtue and punish a kinsman’s crime—state before self; that law does not change.”

sentences.zh: 昔漢初興，多王子弟至於太彊，輒爲不軌，上則幾危社稷，下則骨肉相殘，其後懲戒，以爲大諱。

translations.literal: In olden times at the first rise of Han there were many kings, sons and younger brothers, down to excessive strength; then they were not law-abiding—above they almost endangered the altars of soil and grain, below flesh and bone slew one another; afterward taking warning, they made it a great taboo.
translations.idiomatic: “Early Han princes grew too strong, nearly toppled the throne, and turned on one another—later dynasties took warning.”

sentences.zh: 自光武以來，諸王有制，惟得自娛於宮內，不得臨民，干與政事，其與交通，皆有重禁，遂以全安，各保福祚。

translations.literal: From Guangwu onward the various kings had regulations: they were only permitted to amuse themselves within the palace, could not oversee the people or meddle in government affairs; association with them was all strictly forbidden—thereby they were wholly secure, each preserving blessing and fortune.
translations.idiomatic: “Since Guangwu, princes lived under strict house arrest—no rule over commoners, no politics, heavy ban on private contacts—and so stayed safe.”

sentences.zh: 此則前世得失之驗也。

translations.literal: This is the verification of gain and loss in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: History proves the point.”

sentences.zh: 近袁紹、劉表各有國土，土地非狹，人衆非弱，以適庶不分，遂滅其宗祀。

translations.literal: Recently Yuan Shao and Liu Biao each had a state territory; their land was not narrow, their crowds not weak—because heir and cadet were not divided, in the end their ancestral sacrifices were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: “Yuan Shao and Liu Biao were strong yet ruined themselves by blurring heir and younger son.”

sentences.zh: 此乃天下愚智，所共嗟痛。

translations.literal: This is what fools and wise of the under Heaven together sigh over in pain.
translations.idiomatic: “The world still groans over that lesson.”

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝覽古戒今，防芽遏萌，慮於千載。

translations.literal: The late emperor surveyed antiquity and guarded the present, prevented the sprout and stopped the bud, thinking a thousand years ahead.
translations.idiomatic: “Our late emperor read history, nipped intrigue in the bud, and thought a thousand years ahead.”

sentences.zh: 是以寢疾之日，分遣諸王，各早就國，詔策殷勤，科禁嚴峻，其所戒勑，無所不至，誠欲上安宗廟，下全諸王，使百世相承，無凶國害家之悔也。

translations.literal: Therefore on the days when he lay ill he separately dispatched the various kings, each to go early to his state; the edicts and rescripts were earnest, the prohibitions and restrictions severe, and in what he warned and charged there was nothing not reached—truly he desired above to secure the ancestral temples and below to preserve the various kings, causing a hundred generations to inherit in succession without the regret of a state brought to harm and a house injured.
translations.idiomatic: “On his sickbed he sent every prince to his fief with stern edicts—he meant to secure temple and family for generations.”

sentences.zh: 大王宜上惟太伯順父之志，中念河間獻王、東海王彊恭敬之節，下當裁抑驕恣荒亂以爲警戒。

translations.literal: The great king ought above to ponder Grand Uncle Bo's intent in yielding to his father, in the middle recall the respectful demeanor of Prince Xian of Hejian and Prince Qiang of Donghai, and below ought to restrain arrogance, self-indulgence, wastefulness, and disorder to take them as warning and guard.
translations.idiomatic: “You should think of Taibo’s deference, of Han’s model princes, and rein in pride before it becomes Sun Ba’s disaster.”

sentences.zh: 而聞頃至武昌以來，多違詔勑，不拘制度，擅發諸將兵治護宮室。

translations.literal: But your servant has heard that since coming lately to Wuchang you have often disobeyed edicts and commands, not kept to institutions, and on your own authority deployed various generals' troops to work on and guard the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: “Yet since you reached Wuchang you have ignored edicts, called up troops on your own, and put them to building your palace.”

sentences.zh: 又左右常從有罪過者，當以表聞，公付有司，而擅私殺，事不明白。

translations.literal: Again when attendants and followers at your side committed offenses, it ought to be reported in a memorial and publicly handed to the responsible officials, yet you on your own privately killed them—the affair was not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: “When attendants broke the law you should have reported them to the ministries; instead you executed them secretly.”

sentences.zh: 大司馬呂岱親受先帝詔勑，輔導大王，旣不承用其言，令懷憂怖。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Lü Dai personally received the late emperor's edicts and commands to tutor and guide the great king; since you do not accept and employ his words, he is left harboring worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: “Grand Marshal Lü Dai holds your father’s charge to guide you; your defiance terrifies him.”

sentences.zh: 華錡先帝近臣，忠良正直，其所陳道，當納用之，而聞怒錡，有收縛之語。

translations.literal: Hua Qi was a close minister of the former emperor, loyal, good, and straight; what he stated ought to be accepted and employed—yet your servant hears you were angry at Qi and had words of arresting and binding.
translations.idiomatic: “Hua Qi spoke truth for the late emperor; you answered with threats to bind him.”

sentences.zh: 又中書楊融，親受詔勑，所當恭肅，云『正自不聽禁，當如我何』？

translations.literal: Again Palace Secretary Yang Rong personally received edicts and commands; he ought to have been treated with reverent awe—yet it is said he said, "If I simply do not listen to the prohibitions, what can he do to me?"
translations.idiomatic: “Palace Secretary Yang Rong bore an imperial order; rumor says he sneered, ‘If I ignore the rules, what can he do?’”

sentences.zh: 聞此之日，大小驚怪，莫不寒心。

translations.literal: On the day your servant heard this, great and small were startled and strange; none did not feel cold at heart.
translations.idiomatic: “When that line spread, every official shuddered.”

sentences.zh: 里語曰：『明鏡所以照形，古事所以知今。

translations.literal: A village saying says, "The bright mirror is that whereby one illuminates the form; old affairs are that whereby one knows the present."
translations.idiomatic: “As the proverb says, the mirror shows the face; history shows the present.”

sentences.zh: 』大王宜深以魯王爲戒，改易其行，戰戰兢兢，盡敬朝廷，如此則無求不得。

translations.literal: " The great king ought deeply to take the Prince of Lu as a warning, change and alter his conduct, tremble with fear, and exhaust reverence toward the court—thus there will be nothing sought that is not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: “Take Sun Ba as your warning, change your ways, fear the throne, and you may yet keep everything you seek.”

sentences.zh: 若棄忘先帝法教，懷輕慢之心，臣下寧負大王，不敢負先帝遺詔，寧爲大王所怨疾，豈敢忘尊主之威，而令詔勑不行於藩臣邪？

translations.literal: If you cast aside and forget the former emperor's laws and teachings and harbor a mind of slighting and arrogance, your ministers would rather betray the great king than dare betray the late emperor's testamentary edict; they would rather be resented and hated by the great king than dare forget the awe of honoring the ruler and cause edicts and commands not to be carried out on a vassal minister, would they?
translations.idiomatic: “Ignore your father’s law and we will obey him, not you—we would rather earn your hatred than let your defiance stand.”

sentences.zh: 此古今正義，大王所照知也。

translations.literal: This is the righteous principle of past and present, what the great king clearly knows.
translations.idiomatic: “That is the justice every age knows.”

sentences.zh: 夫福來有由，禍來有漸，漸生不憂，將不可悔。

translations.literal: As for fortune, it comes with a cause; as for calamity, it comes by degrees; if degrees arise and you do not worry, there will be no remorse possible.
translations.idiomatic: “Fortune has roots; disaster creeps in degree by degree—ignore the first step and there is no turning back.”

sentences.zh: 向使魯王早納忠直之言，懷驚懼之慮，享祚無窮，豈有滅亡之禍哉？

translations.literal: If the Prince of Lu had early taken words of loyalty and uprightness and harbored a mind of alarm and fear, would he not have enjoyed blessing without end—how could there have been the disaster of extinction?
translations.idiomatic: “Had Sun Ba listened while there was time, he would still be alive.”

sentences.zh: 夫良藥苦口，惟疾者能甘之。

translations.literal: Good medicine is bitter to the mouth—only the sick can sweeten it.
translations.idiomatic: “Bitter medicine helps only the patient who swallows it.”

sentences.zh: 忠言逆耳，惟達者能受之。

translations.literal: Loyal words grate on the ear—only the perspicacious can receive them.
translations.idiomatic: “Harsh counsel helps only the ruler wise enough to hear it.”

sentences.zh: 今者恪等慺慺欲爲大王除危殆於萌芽，廣福慶之基原，是以不自知言至，願蒙三思。」

translations.literal: " Now Ke and the others earnestly wish for the great king to remove peril and danger in the sprouting stage and broaden the foundation of blessing and fortune—therefore they do not know they have reached the limit of speech; may you favor them with threefold reflection."
translations.idiomatic: “We plead only to cut your risk at the root; forgive our bluntness and think thrice.”

sentences.zh: 奮得牋懼，遂移南昌，游獵彌甚，官屬不堪命。

translations.literal: Fen, receiving the note, was afraid; thereupon he moved to Nanchang, and roaming and hunting became still more extreme; his officials could not bear the orders.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen took fright, moved to Nanchang, and hunted harder than ever while his staff groaned under his whims.

sentences.zh: 及恪誅，奮下住蕪湖，欲至建業觀變。

translations.literal: When Ke was executed, Fen came down and lodged at Wuhu, wishing to go to Jianye to observe the change.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Ke’s murder he camped at Wuhu, eyeing a march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 傅相謝慈等諫奮，奮殺之。

translations.literal: Tutor Xie Ci and others remonstrated Fen; Fen killed them.
translations.idiomatic: His tutors Xie Ci and others remonstrated; he executed them.

sentences.zh: 〈慈字孝宗，彭城人，見《禮論》，撰《喪服圖及變除》行於世。〉

translations.literal: 〈Ci, courtesy name Xiaozong, was a man from Pengcheng; see the Li lun; he composed Mourning Garment Charts and Changes in Removal, current in the world.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xie Ci, courtesy name Xiaozong, came from Pengcheng, wrote ritual treatises still in circulation.〉

sentences.zh: 坐廢爲庶人，徙章安縣。

translations.literal: He was by sitting stripped to commoner status and moved to Zhang'an county.
translations.idiomatic: He was degraded to commoner rank and banished to Zhang’an county.

sentences.zh: 太平三年，封爲章安侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping he was enfeoffed as marquis of Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping 3 restored him as marquis of Zhang’an.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》載亮詔曰：「齊王奮前坐殺吏，廢爲庶人，連有赦令，獨不見原，縱未宜復王，何以不侯？

translations.literal: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan carries Liang's edict: "Prince of Qi Fen earlier by sitting killed clericals, was stripped to commoner; though successive amnesty orders have come, he alone has not been forgiven—granting he ought not yet be restored as prince, how can he not be a marquis?
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan quotes Sun Liang: “Sun Fen killed officials and was cast out; amnesties passed him by—if not a prince, why not a marquis?”

sentences.zh: 又諸孫兄弟作將，列在江渚，孤有兄獨爾云何？

translations.literal: " Again the various Sun brothers serve as generals, arrayed along the river islets; I alone have an elder brother—how can that be?"
translations.idiomatic: “Other Suns command the river—why is my brother alone disgraced?”

sentences.zh: 」有司奏可，就拜爲侯。〉

translations.literal: " The responsible officials memorialized assent; he thereupon went and was invested as marquis.〉
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved and Sun Fen received the seal.〉

sentences.zh: 建衡二年，孫皓左夫人王氏卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianheng, Sun Hao's left consort Lady Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianheng 2: Sun Hao’s senior consort Lady Wang died.

sentences.zh: 皓哀念過甚，朝夕哭臨，數月不出，由是民間或謂皓死，訛言奮與上虞侯奉當有立者。

translations.literal: Hao's grief and longing were excessive; morning and evening he wailed at the catafalque, and for several months did not go out—whereby among the people some said Hao was dead, and false rumor had it that Fen and Marquis of Shangyu Feng were those who ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao mourned so wildly that he vanished from court for months; rumor said he was dead and named Sun Fen or Sun Feng of Shangyu as the next ruler.

sentences.zh: 奮母仲姬墓在豫章，豫章太守張俊疑其或然，掃除墳塋。

translations.literal: Fen's mother Lady Zhongji's tomb was in Yuzhang; the Administrator of Yuzhang, Zhang Jun, suspected it might be so and swept the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen’s mother was buried in Yuzhang; Prefect Zhang Jun swept her tomb, hedging in case the rumor was true.

sentences.zh: 皓聞之，車裂俊，夷三族，誅奮及其五子，國除。

translations.literal: When Hao heard it, he tore Jun apart with chariots, exterminated three clans, executed Fen and his five sons, and abolished the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao had Zhang Jun torn between carts, extirpated three clans, killed Sun Fen and five sons, and erased the princedom.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：豫章吏十人乞代俊死，皓不聽。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan states: Ten clerks of Yuzhang begged to die in Jun's place; Hao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Ten Yuzhang clerks offered to die for Zhang Jun; Sun Hao refused.

sentences.zh: 奮以此見疑，本在章安，徙還吳城禁錮，使男女不得通婚，或年三十四十不得嫁娶。

translations.literal: For this Fen came under suspicion; originally he was at Zhang'an, was moved back to the city of Wu and confined in fetters, causing males and females not to be able to intermarry, some reaching thirty or forty years without being able to marry or take wives.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen was then suspected, moved from Zhang’an to Wu city under house arrest, and his household barred from marriage until some children were past thirty.

sentences.zh: 奮上表乞自比禽獸，使男女自相配偶。

translations.literal: Fen submitted a memorial begging to compare himself to birds and beasts, letting males and females mate among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He begged in a memorial to be treated like livestock free to breed among themselves.

sentences.zh: 皓大怒，遣察戰齎藥賜奮，奮不受藥，叩頭千下，曰：「老臣自將兒子治生求治，無豫國事，乞丐餘年。

translations.literal: Hao was greatly angry, dispatched Inspector of Warfare to bring poison and bestow it on Fen; Fen would not accept the medicine, knocked his head a thousand times, and said, "Your old servant will himself lead his sons in managing life and seeking order; I have not interfered in state affairs; I beg the leavings of years."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao sent an “inspector of warfare” with poison; Sun Fen refused, kowtowed a thousand times, and swore he minded only his sons’ livelihood and never politics, pleading for a few more years.

sentences.zh: 」皓不聽，父子皆飲藥死。

translations.literal: " Hao would not listen; father and sons all drank the medicine and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ignored him; father and sons drank the draught and died.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：建衡二年至奮之死，孫皓即位，尚猶未乆。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: From the second year of Jianheng to Fen's death, Sun Hao had assumed the throne and it was still not long.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: from Jianheng 2 to Sun Fen’s death Sun Hao had reigned only a short while.

sentences.zh: 若奮未被疑之前，兒女年二十左右，至奮死時，不得年三十四十也。

translations.literal: If before Fen came under suspicion the sons and daughters were about twenty in age, by the time of Fen's death they could not have reached thirty or forty.
translations.idiomatic: If the children were about twenty when he fell under suspicion, they could not have been thirty or forty when he died.

sentences.zh: 若先已長大，自失時未婚娶，則不由皓之禁錮矣。

translations.literal: If they had already grown up earlier and, missing the proper time, were unmarried and unwed, then it was not because of Hao's confinement in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: If they were already of age before his disgrace, Sun Hao’s marriage ban cannot explain their celibacy.

sentences.zh: 此雖欲增皓之惡，然非實理。〉

translations.literal: This, though wishing to increase Hao's evil, is not solid principle.〉
translations.idiomatic: The tale piles horror on Sun Hao but does not quite add up.〉

translations.literal: 【Evaluation】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：孫登居心所存，足爲茂美之德。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: What Sun Deng stored in his heart was sufficient to be a flourishing and beautiful virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict: Sun Deng’s character was everything a crown prince should be.

sentences.zh: 慮、和並有好善之姿，規自砥礪，或短命早終，或不得其死，哀哉！

translations.literal: Lu and He both had the bearing of loving the good, regulating and grinding themselves—some finished life early by short fate, some did not meet their natural deaths—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lu and Sun He loved learning and honed themselves—one died young, one was destroyed; both stir pity.

sentences.zh: 霸以庶干適，奮不遵軌度，固取危亡之道也。

translations.literal: Ba, by a cadet interfering with the heir, and Fen, not following track and measure, solidly took the road to peril and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ba usurped the heir’s place; Sun Fen scorned the law—each courted ruin by choice.

sentences.zh: 然奮之誅夷，橫遇飛禍矣。

translations.literal: Yet Fen's extermination by execution was encountering flying disaster crosswise.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen’s slaughter was sheer mischance—guilt by rumor and a tyrant’s panic.
